bash <<'BASH'
set -euo pipefail
run=evorto-evo65-reset-smoke
db="$run-db"
ops="$run-ops"
image="$run:local"
for kind in "$db" "$ops"; do
  if docker container inspect "$kind" >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 1; fi
done
docker network create --internal "$run" >/dev/null
cleanup() {
  result=$?
  if [ "$result" -ne 0 ]; then docker logs --tail 20 "$ops" 2>&1 || true; fi
  docker rm -f -v "$ops" "$db" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker network rm "$run" >/dev/null
  docker image rm "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT
bun run env:run -- docker build --platform linux/amd64 --secret id=FONT_AWESOME_TOKEN,env=FONT_AWESOME_TOKEN --tag "$image" . > /tmp/evorto-evo65-smoke-build.log 2>&1
schema_hash="$(docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none "$image" -e 'console.log(new Bun.CryptoHasher("sha256").update(await Bun.file("dist/evorto/ops/schema.mjs").bytes()).digest("hex"))')"
docker run -d --name "$db" --network "$run" --network-alias database \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=schema_owner -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED -e POSTGRES_DB=evorto_reset_smoke \
  postgres:17.11-alpine@sha256:b0f9560a2de083e2cc7382e75f808c7381a32852a7ec49117deedb300e552b24 >/dev/null
for attempt in {1..30}; do
  if docker exec "$db" pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U schema_owner -d evorto_reset_smoke >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
psql_smoke() { docker exec "$db" psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -qAt -U schema_owner -d evorto_reset_smoke "$@"; }
psql_smoke -c "CREATE TABLE public.legacy_staging_sentinel (id bigint); INSERT INTO public.legacy_staging_sentinel VALUES (1);"
docker run -d --platform linux/amd64 --name "$ops" --network "$run" \
  -e APP_REVISION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" -e APP_IMAGE_DIGEST="$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "$image")" \
  -e APP_ENVIRONMENT=staging -e APP_ROLE=ops -e APP_SCHEMA_HASH="$schema_hash" -e WORKER_TRIGGER_MODE=http \
  -e DATABASE_URL=REDACTED \
  -e DATABASE_TLS_REQUIRED=false -e REDACTED \
  -e COCKPIT_TRACES_ENDPOINT=https://fixture.traces.cockpit.fr-par.scw.cloud/otlp/v1/traces \
  -e COCKPIT_TRACES_TOKEN=REDACTED \
  -e STRIPE_TEST_ACCOUNT_ID=acct_evo65fixture -e E2E_SEED_KEY=evo65-reset-smoke \
  "$image" >/dev/null
for attempt in {1..30}; do
  if docker exec "$ops" /usr/local/bin/bun -e 'const r=await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:4000/healthz"); if (!r.ok) process.exit(1);' >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
failed_status="$(docker exec "$ops" /usr/local/bin/bun -e '
  const response = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:4000/internal/ops/seed-staging", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ confirmation: "reset-and-seed-staging" }),
  });
  console.log(response.status);
')"
test "$failed_status" = 500
test "$(psql_smoke -c "SELECT to_regclass('public.legacy_staging_sentinel') IS NULL;")" = t
test "$(psql_smoke -c "SELECT to_regclass('public.tenants') IS NULL;")" = t
echo 'Reproduced an incomplete database after a post-reset prerequisites failure.'
psql_smoke -c "CREATE ROLE application_runtime LOGIN PASSWORD 'fixture-runtime';"
for attempt in 1 2; do
  started_at="$(date +%s)"
  docker exec "$ops" /usr/local/bin/bun -e '
    const r = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:4000/internal/ops/seed-staging", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ confirmation: "reset-and-seed-staging" }),
    });
    const data = await r.text();
    console.log(data);
    if (!r.ok) process.exit(1);
  ' | jq -e '.reset == true and .seeded == true'
  test "$(psql_smoke -c "SELECT to_regclass('public.legacy_staging_sentinel') IS NULL;")" = t
  test "$(psql_smoke -c "SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE domain = 'staging.evorto.app';")" = 1
  elapsed_seconds="$(( $(date +%s) - started_at ))"
  test "$elapsed_seconds" -lt 300
  test "$(psql_smoke -c "SET ROLE application_runtime; SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE domain = 'staging.evorto.app';")" = 1
  printf 'Seeded and verified runtime role access in %s seconds.\n' "$elapsed_seconds"
  psql_smoke -c 'CREATE TABLE public.legacy_staging_sentinel (id bigint); INSERT INTO public.legacy_staging_sentinel VALUES (1);'
done
echo 'Verified the release image resets and reseeds disposable PostgreSQL twice.'
BASH

I checked the reset timing and recovery concern on the reviewed release image. The ops endpoint hit a real prerequisites failure after dropping the schema in disposable PostgreSQL. After restoring the missing runtime role, the same endpoint rebuilt the schema, recreated the seeded staging tenant and granted the runtime role access in 8 seconds. A second full reset succeeded in 7 seconds. Scaleway currently assigns the private staging ops container 300 seconds per request.

The rollout still has a short period where the existing web and worker can encounter an incomplete database. The runbook documents that window and the retry behavior. The first authorized live rollout is still needed to verify hosted timing, all three role digests, readiness, and the success manifest.
BODY
gh pr comment 239 -R evorto-app/app --body-file "$body_file"

    echo "Both main release gates passed."

done

bash <<'BASH'
set -euo pipefail
merged_revision=fd982dfff9819d1be836680944ba5ea7dc65897d
revision=''
previous=''
while :; do
  current="$(gh api repos/evorto-app/app/commits/main --jq .sha)"
  if [ "$current" != "$revision" ]; then
    git fetch -q origin main
    git merge-base --is-ancestor "$merged_revision" FETCH_HEAD
    git diff --exit-code "$merged_revision" FETCH_HEAD -- .github/workflows/scaleway-staging.yml
    revision="$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)"
    echo "Following main $revision with the reseed workflow."
    previous=''
  fi
  data="$(gh run list -R evorto-app/app --branch main --commit "$revision" --limit 25 --json workflowName,status,conclusion,url,databaseId,event)"
  summary="$(jq -c 'map(select((.workflowName == "PR Quality" or .workflowName == "E2E Baseline") and .event == "push" or .workflowName == "Deploy Scaleway staging")) | sort_by(.databaseId)' <<<"$data")"
  if [ "$summary" != "$previous" ]; then
    jq -r '.[] | [.workflowName,.status,.conclusion,.url] | @tsv' <<<"$summary"
    previous="$summary"
  fi
  if jq -e 'any(.[]; (.workflowName == "PR Quality" or .workflowName == "E2E Baseline") and .status == "completed" and (.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "timed_out"))' <<<"$summary" >/dev/null; then
    exit 2
  fi
  if jq -e '[.[] | select((.workflowName == "PR Quality" or .workflowName == "E2E Baseline") and .conclusion == "success") | .workflowName] | unique | length == 2' <<<"$summary" >/dev/null; then
    echo "Both main release gates passed for $revision."
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 25
done
BASH

A Read Replica is a live copy of a Database Instance that behaves like an Instance, but that only allows read-only connections.
The replica mirrors the data of the primary Database node and any changes made are replicated to the replica asynchronously. Read Replicas allow you to scale your Database Instance for read-heavy database workloads. They can also be used for business intelligence workloads.

A Read Replica can have at most one direct access and one Private Network endpoint. `Loadbalancer` endpoints are not available on Read Replicas even if this resource is displayed in the Read Replica response example.

If you want to remove a Read Replica endpoint, you can use [delete a Database Instance endpoint](#path-endpoints-delete-a-database-instance-endpoint) API call.

Instance Access Control Lists (ACL) also apply to Read Replica direct access endpoints.

# Server Guidelines

## Runtime Architecture

- Prefer Effect and Effect Platform first.
- For Effect v4 reference material, read `repos/effect/LLMS.md` first, then inspect the vendored Effect source under `repos/effect/packages/**` for implementation details, tests, and examples.
- Treat `repos/effect` as read-only reference material. Do not import from it; app code should keep importing from normal Effect packages.
- Organize server capabilities with Effect dependency injection (`Context.Service` + composed `Layer`s).
- Keep service dependencies declared in service definitions; wire app composition with flat `Layer.mergeAll` / `Layer.provideMerge`.
- Keep runtime configuration centralized in `src/server/config/**`; prefer native Effect `Config.*` combinators and resolve optional/default behavior at that boundary.
- Preserve honest config types at the config boundary; prefer `Option` for meaningful absence and only flatten to `undefined` or plain values at the consumer boundary that actually needs it.
- Use Bun-native capabilities when Effect does not provide the needed primitive.
- Do not introduce new Express/Hono server paths.

## API and Validation

- Keep API contracts in Effect RPC + Effect `Schema`.
- Server boundaries must use Effect `Schema` for validated input/output.
- Maintain fully typed input/output boundaries and explicit error mapping.
- Reuse shared RPC contracts from `src/shared/rpc-contracts/**`.

## Auth, Storage, and Integrations

- Keep Auth0 integration aligned with `@auth0/auth0-server-js` architecture.
- For Auth0 SDK calls, keep `Effect.tryPromise(...)` and handle only known SDK/domain errors explicitly.
- Do not convert unknown Auth0/runtime failures into `undefined`/silent fallback values.
- For known Auth0 errors, map to deterministic HTTP/domain responses; for unknown errors, fail and log with context.
- Reference known Auth0 error classes from upstream when defining mappings: [auth0-server-js errors.ts](https://github.com/auth0/auth0-auth-js/blob/main/packages/auth0-server-js/src/errors.ts).
- Prefer Bun-native storage clients (for example Bun `S3Client`) for object storage integrations.
- Keep server-side security headers and webhook protections aligned with current runtime middleware.
- Event registration and add-on charges are Stripe-only. Reject paid event
  configuration or execution without the tenant's connected Stripe account;
  do not add a cash/manual paid-event fallback.
- Treat registration transfer as one inseparable registration/add-on bundle.
  Preserve guest quantity, every included/free/purchased add-on quantity, and
  check-in/fulfillment history. Calculate recipient pricing independently at
  current base prices with recipient-current discounts only, refund each
  original Stripe source exactly, and use database-only completion only when
  the whole bundle is free and no refund is required.
- Google Maps is required production functionality. Cloudflare Images is being
  removed and must not gain new product coupling or release-gate requirements.
- Dispatch each durable email-outbox row at most once. Failed or uncertain
  delivery remains stored and read-only; do not requeue, retry, edit, or resend
  it. An abandoned sending claim becomes delivery-unknown without dispatch.

## Logging

- Pass `disableLogger: true` to Effect HTTP `serve`/`toWebHandler` boundaries.
  ESLint checks explicit options and local constants; the response middleware
  owns sanitized request logging.

- Use Effect platform logging (`Effect.log`, `Effect.logInfo`, `Effect.logWarning`, `Effect.logError`).
- Prefer structured log annotations (`Effect.annotateLogs`) over interpolated log strings.
- Keep raw child-process output and parse/schema errors that echo it out of
  logs and trace exception causes. Keep command identity, exit codes, diagnostic
  labels, and output byte counts.
- Do not use `consola` or direct `console.*` in server runtime code.
- After every server file edit, run `bun run lint` and `bun run format:write`.
- Before calling WebStorm `get_file_problems` on edited server files, run `bun run lint` first.
- Markdown files do not need a WebStorm `get_file_problems` pass.
- After editing a server file, run WebStorm `get_file_problems` on that file when possible before finishing.
# Database Guidelines

- Drizzle schema is the source of truth for persisted shapes.
- Use named imports for Drizzle schema factories. The identifier-length lint rule
  does not follow factories destructured from a namespace object.
- For Drizzle reference material, inspect the vendored upstream source under `repos/drizzle/drizzle-orm/**` first.
- For relation behavior, query builders, dialect details, and type inference, prefer upstream tests in `repos/drizzle/drizzle-orm/tests/**`, `repos/drizzle/drizzle-orm/type-tests/**`, and `repos/drizzle/integration-tests/**` over stale examples.
- Treat `repos/drizzle` as read-only reference material. Do not import from it; app code should keep importing from normal Drizzle packages.
- Prefer inferred Drizzle types across callers; avoid duplicate handwritten DB model types.
- Apply the current Drizzle schema directly for the relaunch using local `db:push` or `db:reset` against the isolated worktree database. Do not add incremental migration artifacts for this cutover.
- Avoid `any`/unchecked casts in query helpers.
- Keep explicit PostgreSQL identifiers within 63 UTF-8 bytes. Declare physical
  table names with `pgTable` or `pgSchema.table`; ESLint rejects `pgTableCreator`
  name transforms. The lint check covers direct declarations and local constant
  names. Verify database behavior through PostgreSQL operations rather than
  column/index metadata mirrors.
- Native PostgreSQL connection retirement must await physical stream closure
  before pool invalidation admits a replacement. A stream marked `destroyed`
  can still be closing. Keep delayed-close regressions for ordinary and
  retained checkouts when changing cancellation or pool lifetime behavior.
- Registration quantity and question text bounds come from `src/shared/registration-quantity-limits.ts` and `src/shared/registration-question-limits.ts`. Keep database checks and varchar sizes aligned with the retained RPC and service validators; never trim input to silently fit storage limits.
- Decode persisted Checkout JSON with `RegistrationCheckoutSnapshotSchema` before resuming any provider request; its shared 100-line bound applies to stored snapshots as well as newly built requests.

- Server-side Effect authorization is authoritative; no PostgreSQL RLS layer is
  planned.

  constraints are integrity safeguards, not authorization mechanisms.

## Drizzle Relations v2 Schema Design Notes

- Define Drizzle relations for query ergonomics, but still define real database foreign keys and constraints in schema tables; relations alone do not create DB constraints.
- For many-to-many, model an explicit junction table and prefer a composite primary key on the pair of foreign keys.
- If using `through(...)` for relation traversal, index each foreign key column and add a composite index on the pair to support both directions and relation resolution efficiently.
- Use relation `alias` when two tables connect in multiple ways (for example `author` and `reviewer`) to avoid ambiguity.
- Only mark a relation as non-optional when the linked row is guaranteed to exist; keep nullable/optional relation types accurate.
- If relation definitions are split with `defineRelationsPart`, merge parts without overwriting table entries and keep one base part that includes all tables for complete type inference.
- Predefined relation `where` filters operate on the target (`to`) table; design polymorphic relation filters with that scope in mind.

Prefer `Effect.gen` for inline Effect code. For reusable functions, prefer

particularly in library implementations and hot paths. Avoid functions that only

style is more readable and easier to maintain than using combinators alone.

Use `Effect.gen` to write code in an imperative style similar to async await.
You can use `yield*` to access the result of an effect.

  yield* Effect.log("Reading file...")

  // Always return when raising an error, to ensure typescript understands that

)

// Use Schema.TaggedError to define a custom error
export class FileProcessingError extends Schema.TaggedError<FileProcessingError>()("FileProcessingError", {
  message: Schema.String
}) {}

# Support reseeding the managed staging database

Staging clears and rebuilds the application objects using the deployment
database role while preserving Scaleway's public schema and extensions.

// The managed database owns public. The ops role owns the application objects
// in it and can rebuild them without removing the schema or its extensions.
export const stagingResetSql = `
  DO $reset$
  DECLARE
    objects record;
  BEGIN
    FOR objects IN
      WITH application_objects AS (
        SELECT kinds.drop_order, kinds.object_kind, relation.relname AS name
        FROM pg_catalog.pg_class AS relation
        JOIN (VALUES
          ('v', 'VIEW', 1),
          ('m', 'MATERIALIZED VIEW', 2),
          ('r', 'TABLE', 3),
          ('p', 'TABLE', 3),
          ('S', 'SEQUENCE', 4)
        ) AS kinds(relation_kind, object_kind, drop_order)
          ON relation.relkind::text = kinds.relation_kind
        WHERE relation.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace
          AND pg_catalog.pg_get_userbyid(relation.relowner) = CURRENT_USER
          AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_depend AS dependency
            WHERE dependency.classid = 'pg_catalog.pg_class'::regclass
              AND dependency.objid = relation.oid
              AND dependency.deptype = 'e'
          )
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 5, 'TYPE', enum.typname
        FROM pg_catalog.pg_type AS enum
        WHERE enum.typnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace
          AND enum.typtype = 'e'
          AND pg_catalog.pg_get_userbyid(enum.typowner) = CURRENT_USER
          AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_depend AS dependency
            WHERE dependency.classid = 'pg_catalog.pg_type'::regclass
              AND dependency.objid = enum.oid
              AND dependency.deptype = 'e'
          )
      )
      SELECT object_kind, string_agg(format('%I.%I', 'public', name), ', ' ORDER BY name) AS names
      FROM application_objects
      GROUP BY drop_order, object_kind
      ORDER BY drop_order
    LOOP
      -- Drop tables together for their mutual foreign keys. RESTRICT prevents
      -- a dependent object outside the reset set from being removed.
      EXECUTE format('DROP %s IF EXISTS %s RESTRICT', objects.object_kind, objects.names);
    END LOOP;
  END
  $reset$;
`;

input.command:
bash <<'BASH'
set -euo pipefail
run=evorto-evo65-managed-smoke
db="$run-db"
ops="$run-ops"
image="$run:local"
for kind in "$db" "$ops"; do
  if docker container inspect "$kind" >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 1; fi
done
docker network create --internal "$run" >/dev/null
cleanup() {
  result=$?
  if [ "$result" -ne 0 ]; then docker logs --tail 20 "$ops" 2>&1 || true; fi
  docker rm -f -v "$ops" "$db" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker network rm "$run" >/dev/null
  docker image rm "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT
bun run env:run -- docker build --platform linux/amd64 --secret id=FONT_AWESOME_TOKEN,env=FONT_AWESOME_TOKEN --tag "$image" . > /tmp/evorto-evo65-smoke-build.log 2>&1
schema_hash="$(docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none "$image" -e 'console.log(new Bun.CryptoHasher("sha256").update(await Bun.file("dist/evorto/ops/schema.mjs").bytes()).digest("hex"))')"
docker run -d --name "$db" --network "$run" --network-alias database \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=provider_owner -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED -e POSTGRES_DB=evorto_reset_smoke \
  postgres:17.11-alpine@sha256:b0f9560a2de083e2cc7382e75f808c7381a32852a7ec49117deedb300e552b24 >/dev/null
for attempt in {1..30}; do
  if docker exec "$db" pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U provider_owner -d evorto_reset_smoke >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
psql_smoke() { docker exec "$db" psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -qAt -U provider_owner -d evorto_reset_smoke "$@"; }
psql_smoke -c "CREATE ROLE schema_owner LOGIN PASSWORD 'REDACTED' NOSUPERUSER; CREATE ROLE application_runtime LOGIN PASSWORD 'fixture-runtime'; GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO schema_owner; CREATE EXTENSION unaccent; CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm; SET ROLE schema_owner; CREATE TABLE public.legacy_staging_sentinel (id bigint); INSERT INTO public.legacy_staging_sentinel VALUES (1);"
docker run -d --platform linux/amd64 --name "$ops" --network "$run" \
  -e APP_REVISION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" -e APP_IMAGE_DIGEST="$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "$image")" \
  -e APP_ENVIRONMENT=staging -e APP_ROLE=ops -e APP_SCHEMA_HASH="$schema_hash" -e WORKER_TRIGGER_MODE=http \
  -e DATABASE_URL=REDACTED \
  -e DATABASE_TLS_REQUIRED=false -e REDACTED \
  -e COCKPIT_TRACES_ENDPOINT=https://fixture.traces.cockpit.fr-par.scw.cloud/otlp/v1/traces \
  -e COCKPIT_TRACES_TOKEN=REDACTED \
  -e STRIPE_TEST_ACCOUNT_ID=acct_evo65fixture -e E2E_SEED_KEY=evo65-reset-smoke \
  "$image" >/dev/null
for attempt in {1..30}; do
  if docker exec "$ops" /usr/local/bin/bun -e 'const r=await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:4000/healthz"); if (!r.ok) process.exit(1);' >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
for attempt in 1 2; do
  docker exec "$ops" /usr/local/bin/bun -e '
    const r = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:4000/internal/ops/seed-staging", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ confirmation: "reset-and-seed-staging" }),
    });
    const data = await r.text();
    console.log(data);
    if (!r.ok) process.exit(1);
  ' | jq -e '.reset == true and .seeded == true'
  test "$(psql_smoke -c "SELECT to_regclass('public.legacy_staging_sentinel') IS NULL;")" = t
  test "$(psql_smoke -c "SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE domain = 'staging.evorto.app';")" = 1
  test "$(psql_smoke -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_extension WHERE extname IN ('unaccent', 'pg_trgm') AND pg_get_userbyid(extowner) = 'provider_owner';")" = 2
  test "$(psql_smoke -c "SET ROLE application_runtime; SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE domain = 'staging.evorto.app';")" = 1
  psql_smoke -c 'SET ROLE schema_owner; CREATE TABLE public.legacy_staging_sentinel (id bigint); INSERT INTO public.legacy_staging_sentinel VALUES (1);'
done
echo 'Verified two real resets with the non-superuser schema role, provider-owned public and extensions, and a separate runtime role.'
BASH

## What changes

The first live rollout deployed ops, then the reset executable failed before worker and web could deploy. Scaleway owns the database and its public schema. Evorto's schema role has write privileges in public and owns the application objects.

The reset now drops app-owned public views, tables, sequences and enums in a single PostgreSQL statement. It preserves the managed schema, extensions and grants. Dependencies outside the reset set block the operation and roll it back. The same private ops endpoint rebuilds the release schema and seeds it after the reset.

## Verification

- PostgreSQL regression test models an unprivileged schema role and checks preservation, failure rollback and a repeated reset.
- The Linux release image completed two resets and reseeds against disposable PostgreSQL with a provider-owned public schema and extensions. The separate runtime role could read the seed afterwards.
- Local lint, formatting, Knope, 2,735 server tests, 1,725 client tests, 388 PostgreSQL tests, Terraform, image and security checks passed. The full browser baseline runs before merge.

entire trail update 01M719PZQKCJA27K0GDTD4P72K --project gh/evorto-app --body 'Main tests and deploys automatically to existing Scaleway staging. No production is provisioned.

Canonical issue: https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-65/restore-automatic-main-to-staging-deployments-without-certification
Owner: Codex in this chat.

PR214 (app/8) and PR215 (app/9) merged without bypass after full local verification, final-head Copilot review and required GitHub checks. Main is 6a8d4db285d8a8dd0b84373c95979d3653a3119f. App delivery uses a private immutable snapshot validated against actual staging container/namespace APIs. No Terraform state or DNS credentials needed for routine releases. Browser test environment is main-only with no approval prompt; the CI Maps key forwarding defect has been fixed with regression coverage.

Full local gate: 2723 server, 1718 client, 387 PostgreSQL and 277 browser/docs tests, plus complete infrastructure/image/security checks. Automatic main quality run42731052185 and baseline42731052075 both passed.

Actual automatic staging run42733377531 initially failed before release because the existing GitHub deployer key expired October17. Replaced GitHub SCW secrets with a verified new key for the same application and staging project, without expanded permissions. New expiry November10,2027. Retrying failed jobs has passed configuration validation and image build; rollout verification remains pending.
https://github.com/evorto-app/app/actions/runs/42733377531

No production, DNS change, Terraform apply/state migration or schema reset occurred. Keep work open until actual role release, manifest and live revision/health verification succeed. Worktree callback-port follow-up is EVO-66, outside this delivery repair.

Verified schema blocker: restored Scaleway backup 7bb031bd-08b3-4532-801d-1ce77aa8dc7e into an isolated temporary PostgreSQL17 instance. Current schema explain reproduces 23 rename/create decisions; a create-only candidate explain (never applied) additionally requires confirmation for16 populated column removals. Backup contains3 tenants,549 users,144 events and1606 registrations. Cloud DB has not been altered. The isolated inspection container was removed after inspection; backup and schema-only decision artifacts remain local with owner-only permissions. Scaleway backup expires2026-12-10.

At the November 10 investigation, web/worker remained on revision d117229 and no successful rollout manifest existed.

On November 20 Lukas confirmed that each normal staging rollout may rebuild and reseed the staging database, including replacement of the existing data. Reuse the incoming release'\''s private staging ops reset after release gates and verify the actual rollout, manifest, revision and readiness. Production keeps its safe schema reconciliation.

PR #239 (app/33) merged without bypass at fd982dfff9819d1be836680944ba5ea7dc65897d after local CI-equivalent checks and final-head Copilot review with no open issues. The release image recovered from a post-reset failure on disposable PostgreSQL and reseeded successfully twice in under ten seconds each. The exact main release gates are running. Keep EVO-65 open until the hosted reset, matching role revisions and digest, health and readiness, and successful manifest are verified.

https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/239
https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/10/changes/app/33

The first hosted deployment of 1e7292c reached the reset executable and failed before web/worker release. Scaleway owns the database/public schema and schema_owner owns the app objects. Follow-up PR #242 (app/36) scopes the reset to app-owned objects in public and preserves the schema, extensions and grants. The packaged fix reset and seeded twice against a schema-only restoration of the prior staging database with provider-equivalent ownership. All full local suites passed, including 388 PostgreSQL and 280 browser/docs tests. GitHub checks and Copilot review are pending.

The `e2e-baseline` environment has 15 test credentials, only main allowed, no reviewers and no wait timer. The existing staging project ID and immutable configuration pointer are set. Anonymous access returns 403. It contains metadata/secret IDs/CA material, not credential values. Temporary inspection/publication keys were revoked.

Live `evorto/platform.tfstate` serial 3060 was privately backed up and not modified. The proposed three-root topology remains unapplied; no production, DNS editing, state migration or schema reset was performed. Existing staging health/version is reachable over IPv4 and previously served `d117229d3d7d357af9f9fc61fdad8d348d6809ea`.

## Verification

Latest full local gate on the forwarding fix: 2723 server tests, 1718 client tests, 387 PostgreSQL integration tests and all 277 browser/documentation tests passed without retries or incomplete outcomes. Frozen install, lint/format/Knope, complete infrastructure validation/scan, Linux/amd64 runtime build/verification, source-map export, SBOM and vulnerability scan passed. Pinned Node 24.22.1 and registered localhost:4200 were used; the original demo web container was restored after every browser gate. No Auth0 client settings were changed.

## Current operational acceptance

Staging workflow is active. Automatic main quality run 42731052185 passed. Automatic baseline 42731052075 started without approval and is executing the full browser suite after the forwarding fix. Its result must pass before deployment.

The quality-completion staging run 42731555975 only resolved eligibility and intentionally skipped its deployment job while the baseline was pending. This is not deployment evidence. Keep this issue in progress until an actual Deploy staging job succeeds, its append-only manifest is written and live web/worker revision/digest plus health checks confirm current main.

content.text:
Staging now rebuilds its database and loads a fresh seed on every successful rollout from `main`. The first successful rollout replaced the existing staging data and deployed `ee520236d33f`. [Deployment and manifest](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/actions/runs/44760521775)

The first attempt exposed a Scaleway schema ownership issue. The follow-up fixed the reset so it clears Evorto’s objects while preserving the managed schema and extensions. All 280 browser tests passed, and I verified that ops, worker, and web are ready on the same image digest. The public `/version`, `/healthz`, and `/readyz` checks passed. [PR #239](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/239) · [PR #242](https://github.com/evorto-app/app/pull/242)

**EVO-65 and Trail 10 are closed.** The pre-reset backup expires November 22. Local verification briefly interrupted some Docker services. I restarted the affected containers and verified both local Evorto web services were ready. [EVO-65](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-65/restore-automatic-main-to-staging-deployments-without-certification) · [Trail 10](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/10)
